1070:     pub(crate) fn call_with_state(&mut self, req: Request<B>, state: S) -> RouteFuture<B, E> {
1071:         macro_rules! call {
1072:             (
1073:                 $req:expr,
1074:                 $method:expr,
1075:                 $method_variant:ident,
1076:                 $svc:expr
1077:             ) => {
1078:                 if $method == Method::$method_variant {
1079:                     match $svc {
1080:                         MethodEndpoint::None => {}
1081:                         MethodEndpoint::Route(route) => {
1082:                             return RouteFuture::from_future(route.oneshot_inner($req))
1083:                                 .strip_body($method == Method::HEAD);
1084:                         }
1085:                         MethodEndpoint::BoxedHandler(handler) => {
1086:                             let mut route = handler.clone().into_route(state);
1087:                             return RouteFuture::from_future(route.oneshot_inner($req))
1088:                                 .strip_body($method == Method::HEAD);
1089:                         }
1090:                     }
1091:                 }
1092:             };
1093:         }
1094: 
1095:         let method = req.method().clone();
1096:         let _ = MethodRouter::<(), Body, Infallible>::classify_request_method(method.as_str());
1097: 
1098:         // written with a pattern match like this to ensure we call all routes
1099:         let Self {
1100:             get,
1101:             head,
1102:             delete,
1103:             options,
1104:             patch,
1105:             post,
1106:             put,
1107:             trace,
1108:             fallback,
1109:             allow_header,
1110:         } = self;
1111: 
1112:         call!(req, method, HEAD, head);
1113:         call!(req, method, HEAD, get);
1114:         call!(req, method, GET, get);
1115:         call!(req, method, POST, post);
1116:         call!(req, method, OPTIONS, options);
1117:         call!(req, method, PATCH, patch);
1118:         call!(req, method, PUT, put);
1119:         call!(req, method, DELETE, delete);
1120:         call!(req, method, TRACE, trace);
1121: 
1122:         let future = match fallback {
1123:             Fallback::Default(route) | Fallback::Service(route) => {
1124:                 RouteFuture::from_future(route.oneshot_inner(req))
1125:             }
1126:             Fallback::BoxedHandler(handler) => {
1127:                 let mut route = handler.clone().into_route(state);
1128:                 RouteFuture::from_future(route.oneshot_inner(req))
1129:             }
1130:         };
1131: 
1132:         match allow_header {
1133:             AllowHeader::None => future.allow_header(Bytes::new()),
1134:             AllowHeader::Skip => future,
1135:             AllowHeader::Bytes(allow_header) => future.allow_header(allow_header.clone().freeze()),
1136:         }

1140: fn append_allow_header(allow_header: &mut AllowHeader, method: &'static str) {
1141:     match allow_header {
1142:         AllowHeader::None => {
1143:             *allow_header = AllowHeader::Bytes(BytesMut::from(method));
1144:         }
1145:         AllowHeader::Skip => {}
1146:         AllowHeader::Bytes(allow_header) => {
1147:             if let Ok(s) = std::str::from_utf8(allow_header) {
1148:                 if !s.contains(method) {
1149:                     allow_header.extend_from_slice(b",");
1150:                     allow_header.extend_from_slice(method.as_bytes());
1151:                 }
1152:             } else {
1153:                 #[cfg(debug_assertions)]
1154:                 panic!("`allow_header` contained invalid uft-8. This should never happen")
1155:             }
1156:         }
1157:     }
1158: }

## Feature Request

### Motivation

`PathDeserializer` doesn't support `deserialize_any` [1](#user-content-fn-1-923a9f7f91b52f0cc41b2b885e1ac5a4) so it doesn't work with things like `time::Date` [2](#user-content-fn-2-923a9f7f91b52f0cc41b2b885e1ac5a4)

### Proposal

Add support for `deserialize_any`. I might be able to look into it in the following days.

### Alternatives

Create a wrapper around the type and force it to use a specific deserializer

      "body": "### Motivation\n\nThere have been requests to convert users' errors into responses in a middleware with access to state (#3211) or propagating errors without converting them into responses first (#2587).\n\nAnother request was to make sure every route uses an authorization extractor (#3221). This could be solved by this by having all handlers return an `AuthorizedIntoResponse` which could be created only with one of the authorization extractors.\n\nOther things this should allow for is returning objects that `impl Serialize` and converting them to `Response`s based on `Accept-Encoding`.\n\nI've also sometimes wanted to be able to transform the returned value before converting it into an HTTP response.\n\n### Current State\n\nCurrently, each `Handler` must return `impl IntoResponse` and the response is automatically immediately converted into `Response` which can then be acted upon by middlewares.\n\nThis architecture lets people to transform only already serialized textual or binary data inside an HTTP response. This is good for things like adding HTTP headers or compression but less so for other transformations like adding a common field to JSON payloads.\n\nSimilarly, `MethodRouter` expects each of its services to return `Response` and `PathRouter` (and `RouterInner`) expects each of its inner services (usually `MethodRouter`s) to also return `Response`.\n\n### Proposal\n\nWe can allow `Handler`s to return any type. Similarly `MethodRouter`, `PathRouter`, and `Router` can then allow any type to be created from a `Request`. In the end we want to call `into_response` on whatever is eventually returned, but that can happen as late as in `Serve` which would require that the `Router`'s response type implements `IntoResponse`.\n\nInstead of generating `Handler` implementation like this:\n\n```rust\nimpl<F, Fut, S, Res, M, $($ty,)* $last> Handler<(M, $($ty,)* $last,), S> for F\nwhere\n    F: FnOnce($($ty,)* $last,) -> Fut + Clone + Send + 'static,\n    Fut: Future<Output = Res> + Send,\n    S: Send + Sync + 'static,\n    Res: IntoResponse,\n    $( $ty: FromRequestParts<S> + Send, )*\n    $last: FromRequest<S, M> + Send,\n{\n    type Future = Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Response> + Send>>;\n\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\nwe can generate:\n\n```rust\n// Added new generic type to `Handler` signifying return type of `Handler::call`\nimpl<F, Fut, S, Res, M, $($ty,)* $last> Handler<(M, $($ty,)* $last,), S, Result<Res, Response>> for F\nwhere\n    F: FnOnce($($ty,)* $last,) -> Fut + Clone + Send + Sync + 'static,\n    Fut: Future<Output = Res> + Send,\n    S: Send + Sync + 'static,\n    Res: 'static, // The returned value does not need implement `IntoResponse`\n    $( $ty: FromRequestParts<S> + Send, )*\n    $last: FromRequest<S, M> + Send,\n{\n    // `Handler::call` will return a future that would resolve to `Res` if all extractors run\n    // successfully or to `Response` created from an extractor rejection.\n    type Future = Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Res, Response>> + Send>>;\n\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\nOf note is that the returned future resolves `Result<Res, Response>` instead of just `Res`. This is because extractors can fail and we need to return something. There are other options for the `Err` variant but this is the simplest solution for the prototype I made.\n\nSimilarly, we can add another generic parameter to `MethodRouter` and `Router` signifying what type will the responses be.\n\nWe would require all handlers in a given `MethodRouter` to resolve to the same type and all `Service`s inside a `Router` to also resolve to the same type. That type can be changed dynamically though using mapping layers.\n\n### Drawbacks\n\nRequiring that services under all router paths may be a bit restrictive and push people to just convert everything into `Response`s anyway. This would probably also introduce new hard-to-debug type errors.\n\nI also think this would be an advanced feature that most users would not need to use often.\n\nSo while we can have an `AdvancedRouter<S = (), Res = Response>` we can still expose `Router<S = ()>` which would work the same way as the `Router` we have today. That way users can decide between the simpler more user-friendly version or the advanced more powerful version. This would make the API surface we need to maintain larger, but the functionality itself would be concentrated only in the general versions of the routers.\n\n### Open Questions\n\nHow to handle extractor rejections. Converting them to `Response`s is simple but we could also return an `enum` containing a variant for each extractor or something like `Box<dyn Rejection>`.\n\nHow to handle default fallbacks. If `Router` returns `Response`s, we have decided that returning an empty 404 response is a sane default. There may not be similar sane defaults for other types. We might require explicit fallbacks.\n\n### Example\n\nI've created a version of this (without having the current and advanced versions side by side) in [this branch](https://github.com/mladedav/axum/tree/dm/generic-responses), where there's also a bit contrived [example](https://github.com/mladedav/axum/blob/a9330c290fb94789a70de33fc38bba4f6390d19c/examples/hello-world/src/main.rs) returning a custom struct which gets turned into `Response` in a later middleware.\n\n### Alternatives\n\nSome of the unlocked functionality can be achieved with response extensions. - **`axum/src/routing/route.rs`**: Added `InfallibleRouteFuture<B>` — a `RouteFuture<B, Infallible>` wrapper that always yields a `Response`.
- **`axum/src/routing/future.rs`**: Exported `InfallibleRouteFuture`.
- **`axum/src/routing/method_routing.rs`**: Implemented `Handler<(), S, B>` for `MethodRouter<S, B, Infallible>` by delegating to `call_with_state` (axum/src/routing/method_routing.rs:7477).

This makes `MethodRouter`s that require state usable as `Router::fallback`, so `Router::new().fallback(get(fallback).fallback(not_found)).with_state(state)` now works with a single `with_state` call.
